title: Word to JPG – Save DOCX Pages as Images Online Free
description: Save each page of a Word document as a JPG image in your browser, with Word's page size, headers and pictures. Several pages in a ZIP. No upload.
heading: Word to JPG
subtitle: Turn each page of a Word document into a JPG picture, several at once in a ZIP; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert DOCX to JPG online without Word: each page of the document becomes its own picture, taken from the layout this site's Word viewer draws, so the page keeps Word's size and the breaks Word saved, along with its header, footer, tables and images. Pages are drawn at 200 dpi on white and saved as JPG; a one-page document gives a single .jpg, and a longer one gives a ZIP with the pages numbered in order. Use a page as a picture in a chat, on a slide or on a website. Works with .docx, .dotx, .docm and OpenDocument .odt files. Your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: The pages are turned into pictures on your device, and the document is not sent to any server.

features.title: One picture per page
features.text: Each page Word marked becomes its own JPG, the same shape as the page, with its header, footer, tables and images in place.

features.title: Numbered in order
features.text: Several pages come in one ZIP, named name-page-01.jpg, name-page-02.jpg and so on.

stepsTitle: How to convert Word to JPG

steps.title: Add the Word file
steps.text: Drop a .docx, .dotx, .docm or .odt file here, or click Choose a file to pick one from your device.

steps.title: Convert
steps.text: Click Convert to JPG; a counter shows which page is being drawn.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Check the preview and download the JPG, or the ZIP with every page.

handles: Input: Word documents and templates (.docx, .dotx, .docm) and OpenDocument text (.odt).
What is drawn on the page: headers and footers, tables, lists and images.
Arabic pages drawn right to left and English pages left to right, as the viewer shows them.
A page longer than Word's page size goes on to the next picture, cut between lines; an .odt file is cut into A4-shaped pictures.
Output: one .jpg for a single page, a ZIP for several.
limits: Each picture shows the page as this site's Word viewer lays it out, which can differ a little from Word; a font missing from your browser is drawn in a stand-in font.
The pictures hold no text: words in a JPG can't be selected or searched.
There is no setting for picture size or quality: pages always come out at 200 dpi and 90% JPG quality.
The older .doc format is not supported; open it in Word or LibreOffice and save it as .docx.
worksBest: CVs and forms to share as pictures
Pages to add to slides or a website
mayNotKeep: Exact line breaks in complex layouts

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I convert a Word document to JPG without Word?
faq.answer: Without Word, a common free way is to save the document as PDF in Google Docs, LibreOffice or Pages, then turn the PDF into pictures. In OpenAnyDoc, choose the .docx file and download a JPG of every page straight away; it is converted in your browser and never uploaded.

faq.question: Will the pictures match the pages in Word?
faq.answer: Nearly. The pictures come from the layout this site's Word viewer makes, and any font your browser lacks is swapped for another. To see the result first, open the file in the Word viewer.

faq.question: How big and sharp are the pictures?
faq.answer: Each page is drawn at 200 dpi and saved at 90% JPG quality, so an A4 page is about 1654 × 2339 pixels and a Letter page about 1700 × 2200: clear on a screen and fine to print. To make the files smaller, use Compress image.

faq.question: Can I copy the text from the JPG?
faq.answer: No. A JPG is only a picture. If you need text that can be searched and copied, use Word to PDF instead.

faq.question: Can I convert an old .doc file?
faq.answer: Not here. The older .doc format can't be opened; save the file as .docx in Word or LibreOffice, then convert that.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
